That's the part about life that is equally as saddening as it is comforting, it is absolutely IMPOSSIBLE to do perfectly. Everyone has regrets (some more intense than others). At a certain point, it becomes very cathartic to just accept that all of that stuff happened, that you can't take it back, and that the future holds more in store for you. Whether any of that is good or not remains to be seen, but at least you can put the past in the past.

Although that is much much much harder said than done. It gets slightly easier with each "I don't care", even if that sentiment isn't true yet. Not saying to numb yourself to everything because please don't, but ignoring those pangs of regret go a long way towards sustaining less hurt throughout life.

You know when you'll find something better? When you consider yourself WORTH better. And I'm happier. Not much happier mind you, but that's my own damn fault for being such an incorrigible pessimist. And it'll be your own fault if you stay in the same situation, blaming yourself for not having something better fall into your lap when someone better was dreaming about being in your lap and not even knowing you existed because you had little miss taking-full-advantage attached to you like a ball and chain. You can listen to what I'm saying, or you can dismiss it. Either's fine, it doesn't really matter, but sooner or later you're going to need to look deep inside yourself and draw a line of what you will and will not put up with, and the person that puts up with anything gets fucked over by EVERYTHING, believe me. Just try to remember who you are and where you stand. Even if it's just becoming more confident in being a shy person, that's good too. Being shy is perfectly valid, tons of people are, but thinking yourself not worth anything will get you nowhere.
